message.content:
**Answer:** The most iconic and widely recognized sculpture of the 19th century is **“The Kiss” (Le Baiser) by Auguste Rodin, completed in 1889**. **Why it stands out** | Feature | Details | |---------|---------| | **Artist** | Auguste Rodin – one of the leading sculptors of the late 19th century, whose work bridged Romanticism and modernism. | | **Date** | 1889 (the year of the Exposition Universelle in Paris). | | **Style** | Realist/Impressionist influence; the piece captures a tender, almost sensual embrace between two figures, rendered with dramatic chiaroscuro and textured surfaces. | | **Cultural Impact** | • The sculpture became an emblem of romantic love and artistic freedom.
• It has been reproduced in countless editions, cast in bronze, marble, and even porcelain.
• It inspired countless artists and remains a staple in art history curricula worldwide. | | **Legacy** | • “The Kiss” is frequently cited as a turning point in sculpture, moving away from idealized forms toward more naturalistic, emotionally charged subjects.
• Its popularity helped cement Rodin’s reputation as a pioneer of modern sculpture. | **Other notable 19th‑century sculptures** | Sculpture | Artist | Year | Significance | |-----------|--------|------|--------------| | **The Gates of Hell** | Rodin | 1880–1917 (unfinished) | A monumental, complex work that influenced modern sculpture and architecture. | | **The Thinker** | Rodin | 1902 (early 20th century) | Though technically from the 20th century, it is often associated with Rodin’s 19th‑century style and remains one of his most famous works. | | **The Sleeping Venus** | Jean-Baptiste-Camille Corot | 1865 | A celebrated example of 19th‑century neoclassical sculpture. | | **The Birth of Venus** (Botticelli) | Botticelli | 1484–1486 (Renaissance) | While not 19th‑century, it continued to inspire 19th‑century artists and was widely reproduced during that era. | **Bottom line:** If you’re looking for the single sculpture that captured the imagination of the 19th‑century public and remains a cultural touchstone today, “The Kiss” by Rodin is the clear winner.
